vacuum_box.name: The Floating Box
vacuum_box.description: A box floats motionless inside a vacuum chamber, with nothing touching it.

questions.prompt: A box floats motionless in a vacuum. What net force acts on it?

known_snares.name: Gravity vanishes in vacuum
known_snares.hint: thinking a vacuum means gravity isn't acting on the box at all

questions.prompt: If the box is motionless, what does that tell you about the forces acting on it?

known_snares.name: Motionless means no forces
known_snares.hint: assuming motionless means there are no forces, rather than balanced forces

sinking_stone.name: The Sinking Stone
sinking_stone.description: A stone released underwater sinks at a constant speed and never gets any faster.

questions.prompt: A stone sinks through water at a constant speed, never speeding up. What does that tell you about the net force on it?

known_snares.name: Constant speed still accelerating
known_snares.hint: believing constant speed means the object is still speeding up because gravity keeps pulling

questions.prompt: If the net force is zero, what must be true about gravity pulling it down versus drag pushing up?

known_snares.name: Gravity always dominates drag
known_snares.hint: assuming gravity must always be stronger than drag once something is moving

hot_cold_chairs.name: Two Chairs, Same Temperature
hot_cold_chairs.description: A metal chair and a wooden chair sit in the same room, but the metal one feels colder to the touch.

questions.prompt: The metal chair feels colder than the wooden one, even though both are the same temperature. What property of the material is actually different?

known_snares.name: Metal is really colder
known_snares.hint: assuming the metal chair must actually be at a lower temperature than the wood

questions.prompt: If both chairs are the same temperature, what is really different about how fast heat leaves your hand when you touch each one?

known_snares.name: Cold flows into the hand
known_snares.hint: thinking cold is being transferred into the hand rather than heat leaving it faster

gps_clock_drift.name: The Drifting Satellite Clock
gps_clock_drift.description: A GPS satellite's onboard clock runs faster than an identical clock on the ground, even though nothing on the satellite is broken.

questions.prompt: GPS satellites sit in weaker gravity than the ground (making their clock run faster) but also move fast enough to add time dilation (making it run slower). Which effect wins, so the net result is the satellite clock ticking FASTER than a ground clock?

known_snares.name: Speed always wins
known_snares.hint: assuming the satellite's high speed always dominates over the weaker gravity effect

questions.prompt: If engineers did NOT correct for this clock drift, would GPS position readings drift toward being more accurate or less accurate the longer the system ran?

known_snares.name: Errors cancel out
known_snares.hint: assuming uncorrected GPS errors would cancel out over time instead of compounding
